open_questions: Whether the January 1988 demo was played on one bass drum or two: the Floyd the Barber tab writes the kick in sixteenths for most of three bars, and Rolling Stone (2016) names his double kick, but no source describes the 1988 kit.

Revolve (Stoner Witch, 1994) and Honey Bucket (Houdini) are not scored: Revolve's tab writes the cowbell and the open hat on every eighth over the snare, three hands, which an overdub would explain but no source confirms; Honey Bucket's intro runs at about 121 and the song at about 176, which one song in the app cannot hold.
Eye Flys (Gluey Porch Treatments, 1987) has only a machine-made tab (Songsterr 7361339).
Boris's last two and a half minutes on the record are not in the tab and are not scored.
Nothing of his playing after 1994 is scored, nor the two-drummer Melvins with Coady Willis from 2006.

identity.name: Dale Crover

evidence.note: Joined the Melvins in 1984 from an Iron Maiden cover band, still at school; the band's drummer since.

identity.summary: The Melvins' drummer since 1984, with Buzz Osborne the band's one constant; the drummer on Nirvana's first demo (January 1988), three songs of which are on Bleach.

affiliations.name: Melvins
affiliations.notes: Replaced Mike Dillard in 1984; plays bass in the 1983 line-up with Dillard (2013, 2021); Coady Willis a second drummer from 2006.

affiliations.name: Nirvana
affiliations.notes: The ten-song demo of 23 January 1988 at Reciprocal and that night's show in Tacoma; a west-coast tour with Sonic Youth in August 1990.

affiliations.name: Fecal Matter
affiliations.notes: With Kurt Cobain; bass and drums on the 1986 demo Illiteracy Will Prevail.

contribution.description: With Buzz Osborne the only constant Melvins member since 1984, the heavy, slow drumming at the root of sludge metal and grunge; he drummed Nirvana's first demo, three songs of which are on Bleach. Rolling Stone's 69th greatest drummer: "tom-toms that explode like cannons".

accolades.award: Rolling Stone, 100 Greatest Drummers of All Time (2016), no. 69

common_misconceptions: That Chad Channing or Dave Grohl plays all of Bleach: Floyd the Barber, Paper Cuts and Downer are Crover's, from the January 1988 demo.

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: A big, damped kick hit hard, open toms and a wash of crashes, in a big room
generation_rules: The kick plays the riff; the floor tom stamps with it.
A crash on the 1, open hats on the beat or the "and"s.
Half time with the snare on 3 at the slow and fast tempos alike.
Let the backbeat move where the riff moves it.
avoid: Busy linear fills over a held groove

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: Kiss Alive! and Zeppelin, a jazz teacher's rudiments and a Carmine Appice book, slowed to a crawl for the Melvins.

traditions.impact: "I learned how to play drums from listening to Kiss Alive! and playing along with that record."

traditions.tradition: The new wave of British heavy metal
traditions.impact: His listening in Aberdeen before the Melvins, "fast and aggressive"; he joined from an Iron Maiden cover band.
Three years of lessons from Bob Neisinger, a jazz drummer: the Haskell W. Harr Drum Method, "Three Camps", competition pieces; he still warms up on rudiments.

formative_events.event: Joins the Melvins after Mike Dillard leaves, still at school; rehearsals move to his parents' house in Aberdeen.
Drums on Nirvana's ten-song demo at Reciprocal, 23 January, tracked live in a day.

eras.label: The Melvins and Nirvana's demo, 1984-1994
eras.context: Aberdeen, then San Francisco: Gluey Porch Treatments, Ozma, Bullhead, Lysol, then Atlantic (Houdini, Stoner Witch); the Nirvana demo of 1988.
defining_traits: The floor tom with the kick

eras.label: The later Melvins, from 1995
eras.context: Thirty albums and more; two drummers with Coady Willis from 2006; the 1983 line-up with Crover on bass.
eras.style_shift: Recording on a small 1948 Gretsch kit, live on huge drums; with Willis, parts written as mirror images.

evidence.note: The tabs and records give no sign of playing behind the beat; heavy, but on it.

swing.notes: Straight in every song scored here.

dynamics.balance: "You're still playing pretty hard." "Yeah, I try." (MD, 2011)

feel_profile.interaction: Follows Buzz Osborne's riffs note for note on the kick and toms; Osborne describes the songs as built "around distinctive drum patterns developed with Crover".

hand_techniques.name: Rudimental warm-up
hand_techniques.description: Rudiments learned from a jazz teacher, still his warm-up.

foot_techniques.name: The kick on the riff
foot_techniques.description: The kick plays the guitar riff, alone for whole bars in Hooch's verse, in sixteenths under crashes in Floyd the Barber.

devices.description: In Hooch's chorus the snare falls on 2 and 4 in one bar and on 1 and 3 in the next, so the backbeat shifts by a beat with the riff over two bars of 4/4.

searched: Songsterr 11404 (Floyd the Barber), 14263 (Paper Cuts), 73509 (Boris), 73507 (Hooch), 472129 (Night Goat), 43132 (Honey Bucket), 43136 (Revolve), 1055436 (Lizzy), 5857988 (Queen)
Modern Drummer, May 2011; Seattle Weekly, 27 October 2009; Wikipedia (Dale Crover, Melvins, Houdini, Bullhead)
devices_search.note: Revolve's 6/4 and 8/4 bars and Honey Bucket's bar of 6/4 are written meter, not devices. Boris's tom triplets are fills of a bar's fraction, not a cross-rhythm.

voice_language.hihat: Open, on the beat or on the "and"s; the foot on the beat under the crash.
voice_language.snare: Hard backbeats, or half time on 3, or moved where the riff puts it (Hooch, Paper Cuts' second pre-chorus).
voice_language.kick: Plays the riff; in sixteenths under crashes into a solo (Floyd the Barber).
voice_language.toms: The floor tom stamping with the kick; both toms in unison with it (Paper Cuts); "tom-toms that explode like cannons".
voice_language.cymbals: A crash on 1 of nearly every bar; choruses ridden on the crash.

sound_profile.cymbal_character: Big crashes ridden through choruses; a ride for the quieter parts.

sample_hints.bleach_demo: Jack Endino's Reciprocal, 1988: a dry, thick kit hit hard.
sample_hints.houdini: A big room, the crashes washing over the toms.

signature_traits.label: The kick on the riff
signature_traits.description: The kick follows the guitar riff, with or without the snare: bars of kick alone in Hooch's verse, the floor tom stamping with it in Floyd the Barber.

signature_traits.label: Toms like cannons
signature_traits.description: Big open toms in unison with the kick (Paper Cuts) and as the stamp of a riff.

signature_traits.label: Slow and half time
signature_traits.description: Sludge tempos (Boris at 63) and half time with the snare on 3 (Night Goat).

patterns.name: Floyd the Barber, the stamp
patterns.function: A crash and the kick on 1, the open hat and the snare on 2, the floor tom and the kick together on 3, its "and" and 4.

patterns.name: Paper Cuts, the toms with the kick
patterns.function: The tom, the floor tom and the kick together on 1, its "and", the "and" of 2, 3, its "and" and the "and" of 4, the snare on 2 and 4.

patterns.name: Hooch, the chorus
patterns.function: Two bars: the open hat on the "and"s of 2, 3 and 4 with the snare on 2 and 4, then the hat on 1 and 2 with the snare on 1 and 3: the backbeat slides with the riff.

patterns.name: Night Goat, the verse
patterns.function: Half time: quarters on the open hat, the snare on 3 alone, the kick in eighths.

patterns.name: Boris, the riff
patterns.function: Sludge at 63, two bars: crashes on 1 and the "and" of 2, the snare on 1 and the "and" of 3; then the open hat on the "and"s, the snare on 1 and 3.

equipment.label: The Honey Bucket video, 1993
equipment.layout_notes: Black shells with chrome hardware and white coated heads, Tama on the kick head.

equipment.label: The big live kit, 1990s-2000s
equipment.layout_notes: A 20" gong bass drum besides; "the loudest kit I ever had".

equipment.label: The 1948 Gretsch recording kit, from the mid-1990s

evidence.note: Bleach: Crover on three songs from the January 1988 demo, Channing on the rest.
"I learned how to play drums from listening to Kiss Alive! and playing along with that record."
"Fueled by his love for Kiss and Zeppelin" (Rolling Stone, 2016): Led Zeppelin as a band; Bonham its drummer.
His teacher "got me a Carmine Appice book" because he wanted to play rock.
Three years of private lessons in junior high; the years are inferred from his age.
Two drummers in the Melvins from 2006, "mirror image" (Willis is left-handed).

philosophy.idea: Learn by playing along with records you love.
Keep the rudiments up: warm up on them before a show.
